exposure: Autologous umbilical cord blood (UCB) mononuclear cells
cohort: The study included newborn lambs, with birth asphyxia induced by clamping the umbilical cord in 20 lambs and 11 serving as controls, and a subset of asphyxiated lambs (n=8) receiving autologous UCB mononuclear cells.
finding: The administration of autologous UCB mononuclear cells significantly decreased neuronal apoptosis, astrogliosis, and inflammation, and restored normal brain metabolism following perinatal asphyxia in newborn lambs.
